Luna E-6 No.2: Soft-land a camera capsule on the Moon.
The upper stage did not perform the burn needed to leave Earth orbit.
Luna E-6 No.3: Soft-land and photograph the lunar surface.
A guidance problem caused loss of control during launch; the probe did not reach Earth orbit.
Luna E-6 No.6: Land a camera capsule on the lunar surface.
A broken valve mechanism prevented the third-stage engine from reaching full thrust.
Luna E-6 No.5: Demonstrate a soft landing on the Moon.
An electrical-circuit failure shut down the third-stage engine prematurely.
Kosmos 60: Soft-land and send pictures from the surface.
A guidance-system electrical fault prevented the upper stage from sending the craft toward the Moon.
Luna E-6 No.8: Loss of pressure in a nitrogen line prevented third-stage ignition. The spacecraft never reached orbit.
Kosmos 111: Enter lunar orbit and study the Moon.
The upper stage lost roll control and did not fire toward the Moon.
Luna 11: Photograph the surface from lunar orbit and study the Moon’s environment.
Entered orbit and returned scientific data, but an attitude-control problem prevented usable lunar images.
Luna 12: Return detailed photographs of the lunar surface.
Entered lunar orbit and returned surface images, completing the imaging task missed by Luna 11.
Luna 13: Land instruments to study soil and photograph the surface.
Returned surface panoramas and measurements of soil properties after a successful landing.
Luna E-6LS No.112: Test lunar communications for future crewed missions.
Premature third-stage cutoff prevented the spacecraft from reaching Earth orbit.
Luna 14: Test lunar communications and track gravitational effects on spacecraft motion.
Entered lunar orbit and supported communications, gravity and particle investigations.
Luna E-8 No.201: Deliver a mobile rover to explore the lunar surface.
The payload shroud failed during ascent; the rover and launch vehicle were lost.
Luna E-8-5 No.402: Collect lunar soil and return it automatically to Earth.
A guidance-circuit problem prevented the upper stage from firing. The craft did not reach Earth orbit.
Zond 7: Test a circumlunar flight, imaging and guided Earth return.
Flew around the Moon, photographed Earth and Moon, and returned its capsule safely.
Kosmos 300: Collect lunar soil and return it to Earth.
An upper-stage fuel-valve problem prevented the departure burn from Earth orbit.
Kosmos 305: Return a robotic sample of lunar soil.
The upper stage failed to execute the departure sequence; contact was lost and the spacecraft reentered.
Luna E-8-5 No.405: Collect and return material from the lunar surface.
An erroneous command shut down the second stage during ascent, ending the mission.
Zond 8: Test a circumlunar journey and capsule recovery.
Photographed the Moon and returned its capsule to the Indian Ocean after a ballistic reentry.
Luna 18: Land, collect lunar soil and return it to Earth.
Reached lunar orbit, but contact was lost during the landing attempt and no samples returned.
Luna 19: Photograph the surface and investigate lunar gravity and space conditions.
Conducted an extended programme of observations from lunar orbit.
Luna 20: Collect lunar highland material and bring it to Earth.
Landed, collected soil and successfully returned its sample capsule.
Luna 22: Photograph the surface and study composition, radiation and the lunar environment.
Completed its orbital science programme and continued observations beyond the primary mission.
Kaguya: Study the Moon’s surface and gravity with an orbiter and relay satellites.
Completed its lunar observations before a controlled impact at the end of the mission.
Chang’e 1: Map the Moon and study its surface from orbit.
Successfully entered lunar orbit and completed China’s first mission to the Moon.
Chang’e 2: Map the lunar surface and demonstrate improved lunar exploration technology.
Completed its lunar orbital mission before continuing to other destinations.
Chang’e 3: Land instruments and the Yutu rover for surface exploration.
Successfully landed and deployed Yutu; rover mobility was later limited.
Chang’e 5-T1: Rehearsing a return from the Moon
Test a high-speed Earth return after a lunar flyby.
The test capsule returned successfully, supporting later lunar sample-return missions.
Queqiao: Relay communications between Earth and a far-side lander.
Established a communications relay supporting exploration of the lunar far side.
Chang’e 4: First landing on the far side
Land a spacecraft and rover on the lunar far side.
Achieved the first soft landing on the Moon’s far side and deployed Yutu 2.
Chang’e 5: Collect lunar material and bring it to Earth.
Successfully returned samples from the near side of the Moon.
Danuri: Demonstrate lunar-orbit operations and study the Moon.
Entered lunar orbit and began scientific observations as South Korea’s first lunar mission.
Luna 25: A landing attempt ended in orbit
Land near the lunar south-polar region and study the surface.
The spacecraft crashed before its planned soft landing.
Chang’e 6: Collect and return material from the Moon’s far side.
Completed the first return of lunar far-side samples to Earth.
